key_insight: Machine-learning models can accurately predict and help optimize the tensile strength and micro-hardness of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints from welding parameters.
engineering_relevance: The study supports data-driven welding process design, enabling faster parameter selection for stronger, more consistent joints in sustainable manufacturing.
method: Inputs: tool rotational speed, traverse speed, and plunge depth.
Models compared: LR, RF, SVR, XGBoost, and KNN.
Best performers: RF for UTS and SVR-RBF for micro-hardness.
evidence_signal: Using an 80:20 train-test split, RF achieved the lowest UTS test errors (MAE 9.007 MPa, RMSE 12.975 MPa) and SVR-RBF achieved the best micro-hardness accuracy (MAE 0.923 HV, RMSE 1.155 HV).
watch_item: The models were evaluated on experimental data with a limited feature set, so broader validation is needed before deployment across different materials, tool geometries, and welding setups.
paper_title: Explainable machine learning approach for predicting mechanical characteristics of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints
